title: Use what you have
translation: Some people forget how the good rulers of the past governed, don't care that ordinary people are suffering and the country is in a bad way, spend everything on luxury, think they're wonderful, and make a big show of it. They just look thoughtless, and it's depressing.

"From your clothes to your horses and carriages, use what you have. Don't go looking for beautiful things." That's from the house rules Morosuke left his family. And when Emperor Juntoku wrote about life at court, he said: "What the emperor himself wears is best when it is plain."
original: いにしへの{聖|ひじり}の{御代|みよ}の{政|まつりごと}をも{忘|わす}れ、{民|たみ}の{憂|うれ}へ、{国|くに}のそこなはるるをも{知|し}らず、{万|よろづ}にきよらを{尽|つく}して、いみじと{思|おも}ひ、{所狭|ところせ}きさましたる{人|ひと}こそ、うたて、{思|おも}ふところなく{見|み}ゆれ。
「{衣冠|いくわん}より{馬車|うまくるま}に{至|いた}るまで、あるに{随|したが}ひてもちひよ。{美麗|びれい}を{求|もと}むることなかれ。」とぞ{九条殿|くでうどの}の{遺誡|ゆゐかい}にもはべる。
{順徳院|じゆんとくゐん}の、{禁中|きんちゆう}の{事|こと}ども{書|か}かせ{給|たま}へるにも、「おほやけの{奉物|たてまつりもの}はおろそかなるをもてよしとす。」とこそ{侍|はべ}れ。
literal: People who forget even the government of the reigns of the wise (rulers) of old, do not know the people's grief or the country's being harmed, exhaust splendour in everything, think it splendid, and behave as if they own the place: they look, unpleasantly, thoughtless.
'From robes and caps to horses and carriages, use them as they are. Do not seek beauty': so it is in the last instructions of Lord Kujō.
Also in what Retired Emperor Juntoku had written about matters at court, it says: 'The emperor's own garments are considered good when plain.'

notes.text: {所狭|ところせ}し: 'taking up a lot of room', so 'acting grand, overbearing'.
'Unpleasantly, depressingly'. A word that shows the writer's own feeling, not a fact about the people.
Lord Kujō is Fujiwara no Morosuke (908–960), a powerful minister. His 'last instructions' to his descendants, the Kujōdono Ikai, were a famous guide to how a noble family should behave.
Emperor Juntoku (1197–1242) wrote a handbook on court customs, the Kinpishō. Kenkō quotes it as an authority: even an emperor says plain is better.
{奉物|たてまつりもの}: what the emperor wears or uses. たてまつる is a respectful verb for 'to wear' here, and おほやけ means the emperor and the court.
A false friend: here おろそか means 'plain, simple'. Modern {疎|おろそ}か means 'careless, neglected'.
